title: Euclidean and hyperbolic Pythagorean theorem formalizations

problemStatement.formal: v\perp w\Rightarrow \|v+w\|^2=\|v\|^2+\|w\|^2,\quad \operatorname{cosh}(c)=\operatorname{cosh}(a)\operatorname{cosh}(b)\text{ for hyperbolic right triangles}.
problemStatement.plain: Repair the truncated metadata for the Pythagorean theorem track. The Lean support proves the inner-product-space Euclidean theorem and converse, records classical numeric triples, and gives the hyperbolic right-triangle law in a separate zero-sorry development.
whyMatters: The Euclidean theorem is a canonical example of translating geometry into inner-product algebra.
The converse theorem turns the metric identity back into perpendicularity.
The hyperbolic variant shows the same theorem family across geometries without axiom or sorry debt in the declared files.

proven: `pythagorean_theorem` proves the squared-norm identity for perpendicular vectors in the Euclidean plane.
`pythagorean_converse` proves that the squared-norm identity implies perpendicularity.
`hyperbolic_pythagorean` records the hyperbolic right-triangle law `cosh c = cosh a * cosh b`.
open: Future work can connect these algebraic statements to richer geometric constructions and diagrammatic triangle APIs.
knownResults.goal: Present the completed Euclidean and hyperbolic Lean content under a non-truncated, geometry-focused research problem shell.
